What does carpet installation cost in a Shoreline home?

Plan on $4 to $7 per square foot installed in Shoreline, covering the carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away. Typical projects here run $2,000 to $4,500, while a 1,200 sq ft main floor plus a staircase generally comes in between $5,500 and $8,500. The carpet grade you choose moves the number more than anything else — and you choose it from samples laid out in your own house.
Does the mobile carpet showroom cover Shoreline?

Yes — the van works all of Shoreline. It carries 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades, and we set the samples down in the exact rooms you're carpeting so the color reads true in your own light. Before leaving we measure every room and stair and hand you a written price. The visit is free and there is no store to drive to.
What does carpet stretching cost in Shoreline?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Shoreline. A power stretcher pulls ripples, waves and bunched-up trip spots flat again, typically for about a fifth of what replacement would run. If the pile still stands up and you still like the color, stretching is usually the smarter spend.
How much are carpeted stairs in Shoreline?

Stairs start at $18 per step, installed waterfall style or cap-and-band. If your staircase has a landing or pie-shaped winders, those are counted in the written quote from the start — they will not show up later as a surprise charge.
How long will the installation take?

One day covers most Shoreline homes. A rambler's worth of bedrooms plus the hallway is a routine day for our crew; add a staircase, a finished basement and a house full of furniture and the job can run into a second day. Your quote spells out the schedule in writing before we start.
Do your installers handle the furniture?

We move the big pieces — beds, dressers, sofas, tables — on most jobs and return them to their places once the carpet is in. We ask you to pack up the small things first: closet floors, electronics, plants, breakables and anything personal you would rather carry yourself.
Is it better to restretch carpet or replace it?

Restretch when the pile stands up, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — that is a $99-per-room repair instead of a full replacement. Replace when traffic lanes are crushed flat, seams are pulling apart, the backing crumbles, or pet odor has outlived a professional cleaning. We look first and tell you honestly which job yours is.
Which Shoreline neighborhoods do you cover?

All of them — Richmond Beach, Innis Arden, Richmond Highlands, Hillwood, Highland Terrace, Echo Lake, Meridian Park, Westminster Triangle, Parkwood, Ridgecrest, North City, Briarcrest, Ballinger and The Highlands — plus Lake Forest Park, Broadview and the rest of north Seattle and south Snohomish County.
What's the best carpet for a house with pets?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, installed over a moisture-barrier pad. The barrier keeps accidents from ever reaching the subfloor — the true source of odor that will not leave — and solution-dyed fiber tolerates diluted bleach without losing color. The pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot, and it rides in the van so you can see and feel it first.
What warranty comes with the install?

Two layers. OC Flooring backs the workmanship with a 1-year warranty, and the mill backs the carpet itself — typically 10 to 25 years against wear and stains depending on grade. Both go on your written quote. Worth knowing: some mill warranties require a minimum pad grade, which is one more reason all three pad grades come along to the measure.
